newsitem.title: USA: Minn. Fed sees slowing job growth in Upper Midwest.
newsitem.headline: Minn. Fed sees slowing job growth in Upper Midwest.

text.p: A slowing in employment growth that began last year in the Upper Midwest region of the United States will likely continue through 1997, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis' forecasting models.

The Minneapolis Fed, which serves Minnesota, Montana, North and South Dakota, part of Wisconsin and Michigan's Upper Peninsula, forecast employment growth of 1.2 percent in the region in 1997 on a fourth-quarter to fourth-quarter basis.
That would be a deceleration from the 1.8 percent growth rate recorded for 1996 and the 2.0 percent rate for 1995.

"Forecasting models indicate a slackening in the employment growth of the national economy as well, and reveal that the district's fall-off has been somewhat greater than the nation's," it said in a statement. "One explanation is that labor availability is restraining hiring more in the district than the nation."

It said the regional forecast is based on an expectation of slowing in the national economy, where it saw nonfarm employment growth slowing to 0.8 percent in 1997, then picking up to a 1.7 percent rate in 1998.
The economy added jobs at a 2.4 percent rate in 1996 with monthly job creation averaging 213,667, Labor Dept data show.
